answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by treating reputation as a finite, hard-earned resource. A new identity appears like a faint shadow in the umber dusk, possessing no established weight in the system. It must contribute consistently across many epochs; its record acts like a slow-moving glacier, carving irreversible trust into the network. Only when a node proves its history—rising like a plume of steam above the noise—does it gain voting power. This ensures the economy stays decentralized rather than being flooded by mass-generated, low-effort accounts.
